Client.title: Client
Client.description: Represents a client using the LexConnect platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Client entity.

Lawyer.title: Lawyer
Lawyer.description: Represents a lawyer on the LexConnect platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Lawyer entity.

specializations.description: Array of specializations of the lawyer.

experienceYears.description: Years of experience of the lawyer.

availableTimes.description: Available consultation times of the lawyer.

qualifications.description: References to Qualification documents. (Relationship: Lawyer 1:N Qualification)

Consultation.title: Consultation
Consultation.description: Represents a consultation between a client and a lawyer.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Consultation entity.

dateTime.description: Date and time of the consultation.

type.description: Type of consultation (video, audio, chat, document analysis).

status.description: Status of the consultation (pending, confirmed, completed, cancelled).

offer.description: WebRTC session description offer from the caller.

answer.description: WebRTC session description answer from the callee.

Document.title: Document
Document.description: Represents a document uploaded or exchanged during a consultation.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Document entity.

uploaderId.description: Reference to the Uploader (Client or Lawyer).

fileType.description: Type of the document file (PDF, DOCX, JPG).

uploadDateTime.description: Date and time when the document was uploaded.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Qualification entity.

documentType.description: Type of qualification document (passport, license, certification)

Message.title: Message
Message.description: Represents a chat message within a consultation.

consultationId.description: The ID of the consultation this message belongs to.

senderId.description: The UID of the user who sent the message.

text.description: The content of the chat message.

timestamp.description: The time the message was sent.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support the LexConnect application's requirements for online legal consultations and user management, prioritizing security and scalability. Authorization Independence is achieved through denormalization, specifically within the `consultations` collection. Access is modeled using path-based ownership for user-specific data.

The `clients/{clientId}` and `lawyers/{lawyerId}` collections store profile information for each type of user, segregated to maintain a homogeneous security posture. 

Consultations are structured under `/consultations/{consultationId}`, with denormalized `clientId` and `lawyerId` fields to enable authorization rules without needing `get()` calls. Documents associated with consultations are nested under `/consultations/{consultationId}/documents/{documentId}`.

**Authorization Independence:** The denormalization strategy is evident in the `consultations` collection, where `clientId` and `lawyerId` are explicitly stored, enabling direct rule evaluation without fetching related user documents. This is critical for atomic operations and avoids hierarchical authorization dependencies.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
*   List operations are secured using structural segregation. Each collection (`clients`, `lawyers`, `consultations`) has a specific security posture that restricts unauthorized listing.
*   The membership map approach for collaborative access allows listing documents within a consultation only to its participants, ensuring secure access control.
